{{verse|chapter=13|verse=31}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō the 6 Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}An other parable he propo{{ls}}ed vnto them, {{ls}}aying, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 4, 30. Luc. 13, 18.''}}* The kingdom of heauen is like to a mu{{ls}}tard-{{ls}}eede, vvhich a man tooke and {{ls}}ovved in his field. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=32}} Which is the {{sup|‖}} lea{{ls}}t {{ls}}urely of al {{ls}}eedes: but vvhen it is grovven, it is greater then al herbes, and is made a tree, {{ls}}o that the foules of the aire come, and dvvel in the branches thereof. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=33}} An other parable he {{ls}}pake to them, The kingdom of heauen is like to leauen, vvhich a vvoman tooke and hid in three mea{{ls}}ures of meale, vntil the vvhole vvas leauened.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=34}} Al the{{ls}}e things {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}pake in parables to the multitudes, and vvithout parables he did not {{ls}}peake to them: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=35}} that it might be fulfilled vvhich vvas {{ls}}poken by the Prophet {{ls}}aying, I wil open my mouth in parables, ''I wil vtter things hidden from the foundation of the vvorld''.⊣ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''P{{ls}}a. 77, 2.''}}

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=36}} Then hauing dimi{{ls}}{{ls}}ed the multitudes, he came into the hou{{ls}}e, and his Di{{ls}}ciples came vnto him, {{ls}}aying, Expound vs the parable of the cockle of the field. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=37}} Who made an{{ls}}vver and {{ls}}aid to them, He that {{ls}}oweth the good {{ls}}eede, is the Sonne of man. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=38}} And the field, is the vvorld. And the good {{ls}}eede: the{{ls}}e are the childrē of the kingdom. And the cockle: are the children of the vvicked one. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=39}} And the enemie that {{ls}}ovved them, is {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not God then, but the Diuel is the author of all euil.}}∷ the deuil. But the harue{{ls}}t, is the ende of the vvorld. And the reapers, are the Angels. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=40}} Euen as cockle therfore is gathered vp, and burnt vvith fire: {{ls}}o {{ls}}hal it be in the ende of the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=41}} The Sonne of man {{ls}}hal {{ls}}end his Angels, and they {{ls}}hal gather out of his kingdom al {{ls}}candals, and them that vvorke iniquitie: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=42}} and {{ls}}hal ca{{ls}}t them into the furnace of fire, There {{ls}}hal be vveeping and gna{{ls}}hing of teeth. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=43}} Then {{ls}}hal the iu{{ls}}t {{ls}}hine as the {{ls}}unne, in the kingdom of their father. He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=44}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel for Virgins & other holy women.}}The kingdom of heauen is like a trea{{ls}}ure hidden in a field. vvich a man hauing found, did hide it, and for ioy thereof goeth, and {{ls}}elleth al that he hath, and byeth that field. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=45}} Againe the kingdom of heauen is like to a marchant man, {{ls}}eeking good pearles. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=46}} And hauing found one precious pearle, he vvent his vvay, and {{ls}}old al that he had, and<noinclude>{{continues|bought}}</noinclude>
